units.title: Software Project Management Concepts
topics: Introduction: project, software project and project management
Importance of and problems in software project management
Activities and the process of software project management
Characteristics of a good project manager

sections.title: Introduction: project, software project and project management
Importance of and problems in software project management
Activities and the process of software project management
Characteristics of a good project manager

summary: A project is a temporary, unique effort with objectives and constraints; a software project delivers software and its supporting documentation.
Software projects are harder to manage than conventional ones because the product is invisible, complex, constantly changing and difficult to estimate.
SPM matters because it provides plans, control, early warning and quality assurance; typical problems are poor requirements, estimation, scope creep and weak risk management.
SPM activities run from feasibility to closure, within a plan-do-monitor-replan cycle and the PMBOK knowledge areas.
A good project manager combines leadership, communication, planning, negotiation and integrity; success is measured by value delivered and a team that remains intact.
Planning follows the Step Wise outline and produces several plans, beginning with a clear scope statement.

units.title: Software Project Scheduling
topics: PERT: program evaluation and review technique

sections.title: PERT: program evaluation and review technique

summary: Activity planning supports feasibility checks, resource allocation, costing, co-ordination and control; a WBS decomposes deliverables to work packages (100% rule).
Network models show dependencies; AON with FS, SS, FF, SF relationships and lags is the modern standard; AOA needs dummy activities.
CPM computes the critical path with a forward and a backward pass; float shows scheduling freedom.
PERT uses three-point estimates and gives probabilities of meeting a date.
Only shortening the critical path shortens the project: crash the cheapest critical activity, or fast-track.
Gantt charts communicate schedules; earned value measures real progress against cost and time.

units.title: Software Estimation Techniques
summary: Over-estimation wastes resources (Parkinson's law) and under-estimation harms quality and morale (Brooks' law); estimates are ranges that narrow over time (cone of uncertainty).
Estimates are based on size, productivity from historical data, and adjustment factors.
Experience-based methods are expert judgement, Delphi and analogy; decomposition methods are bottom-up and top-down; algorithmic methods are function points and COCOMO.
Function points measure user functionality independent of language; COCOMO converts KLOC to effort, time and staffing with b > 1.
Use several techniques, keep records and re-estimate at milestones.

units.title: Software Evaluation and Costing
topics: Project evaluation: strategic and technical assessment
Selection of an appropriate project report
Project approach: choosing technologies and process models

sections.title: Project evaluation: strategic and technical assessment
Selection of an appropriate project report
Project approach: choosing technologies and process models

summary: Evaluation asks if a project is strategically aligned, technically feasible and economically worthwhile.
CBA lists costs and benefits; a cash flow forecast shows when they occur; NPV and IRR use the time value of money, payback and ROI do not.
Risk evaluation uses sensitivity analysis, expected values and risk-adjusted discount rates.
The project report presents the findings to the sponsor in a structure suited to its readers.
The project approach covers build-or-buy, technology choice and process model; the right model depends on requirement and technology uncertainty.

units.title: Risk Management
topics: A framework for dealing with risk

sections.title: A framework for dealing with risk

summary: Risk is an uncertain event with probability and impact; exposure combines them. Categories include requirements, estimation, technology, people, organisation and external risks.
The framework is identification, assessment, planning and monitoring, kept in a risk register and repeated throughout the project.
Qualitative matrices and quantitative exposure rank risks; responses are avoid, mitigate, transfer or accept, supported by contingency plans and reserves.
Schedule risk is assessed with PERT, near-critical paths, Monte Carlo simulation and buffers.

units.title: Software Quality Management
topics: Place of software quality in software planning
Software quality assurance and process maturity

sections.title: Place of software quality in software planning
Software quality assurance and process maturity

summary: Quality means fitness for use and conformance to measurable requirements; defects cost more the later they are found.
ISO 9126 divides product quality into six characteristics with sub-characteristics and metrics, and has been succeeded by ISO 25010.
Quality is planned: quality requirements, a quality plan, reviews and tests, quality gates and metrics such as DRE.
TQM builds quality into all processes through customer focus, involvement and PDCA; Six Sigma reduces defects statistically with DMAIC.
SQA, ISO 9001 and CMMI organise quality at the level of the organisation.

units.title: Software Configuration Management
topics: Case study: version control tools (Git, CVS, SVN)

sections.title: Case study: version control tools (Git, CVS, SVN)

summary: SCM controls change so that every version is identified, traceable and reproducible.
Configuration items under a repository, frozen as baselines, change only through change control.
Version control systems are local, centralised (CVS, SVN) or distributed (Git); the copy-modify-merge model dominates, with branches and tags.
The SCM process is identification, version control, change control, audit and status accounting, with build and release management.
Change control passes each request through impact analysis and a Change Control Board.
FCA and PCA verify product and baseline; status reports give the audit trail.
Git is the leading tool; SVN is centralised with atomic commits; CVS is a legacy predecessor.
